Metadata.title: Pierre-Alexandre Monneau — Portfolio
Metadata.description: Freelance JS/TS developer — background and projects.

Hero.pitch: Full-stack JavaScript/TypeScript developer, I support the design, development and production launch of digital products.

Parcours.title: From client missions to shipped products
Parcours.intro: 7 years of full-stack and tech lead experience, freelance web and mobile developer based in Lille, France.

recordair.context: Three-sided studio booking marketplace, designed and built end-to-end independently: booking flow, studio back-office, real-time messaging and GCP infrastructure. Stripe payments integrated through to capture, webhooks and marketplace commissions.

homeair.context: Home services marketplace built around two journeys, client and provider, with a dual-role account and either direct bookings or applications. Next.js architecture with self-hosted Supabase on GCP, targeting a Go API to progressively evolve the back-end.

ankama.context: Tech lead for a 12-person team on Ankama Launcher: technical steering of sprints, cross-team migrations and developer mentoring. Set up a NestJS API in clean architecture and on-demand personal environments deployable via GitLab CI.

absPreschool.context: Built a CMS platform for a US preschool chain (design excluded), from functional scoping to GCP oversight. Next.js front-end, headless Strapi back-end and a Go adapter API to normalize and expose data from several external sources.

waykonect.context: Platform overhaul within a 6-person team, independently building the Next.js back-office and evolving the React product. Took over an undocumented project, re-integrated it into the AWS infrastructure and created pipeline-deployable test environments.

illicado.context: Designed the Wallet NestJS API covering the full gift card lifecycle within a microservices architecture. Built hexagonal CRUD APIs, revamped the back-office in Vue 3 / Nuxt and set up GitLab CI/CD.

lyreco.context: Front-end lead for a 10-person Scrum team on the B2B e-commerce site: TypeScript migration, legacy refactoring and performance optimization. Set up Jest, linting and Prettier, then trained three developers on TS/JS best practices.

ecommerceClient.context: Independently built e-commerce sites with Next.js in SSR/BFF and a documented hexagonal architecture. Integrated NextAuth, microservices and a GitLab CI/CD pipeline with Ansible provisioning.

adeo.context: Built the ERPC POC within a 4-person team: reworked back-end services in hexagonal architecture and developed NestJS features. Set up KafkaJS for inter-microservice communication, with documentation and automated tests.

sncf.context: Integrated and maintained the React front-end of SNCF's passenger digital platform. Built features with Redux, integrated Drupal templates and wrote refactoring documentation.

phi.context: Independently delivered web and mobile projects for an agency: Express microservices, admin dashboards and Passport.js authentication. Built a React Native app with geolocation, PDF generation and Stripe payments.

clicar.context: Built clicar.com within a two-developer, one-designer team: React front-end and Express.js API. Delivered authentication, the admin dashboard and Docker deployment, and contributed to training and course content.

infoLogiSante.context: Overhauled and integrated the front-end of a business application for the healthcare sector. Fixed bugs, integrated UI and progressively refactored legacy ASP.NET code.

facts: Storybook documentation deployed straight from the stories

Stripe payments with authorization then capture
recordair.note: The most complete project — from idea to a product running in production.

facts: Payment triggered on quote acceptance, plus a reputation system
homeair.note: Live, being polished ahead of a stable production release.

biair.pitch: A curated selection of two-player games, playable on the same device or remotely in real time.
facts: Four games: cards, hangman, dice and charades
Local and real-time remote modes via Supabase Realtime
biair.note: Architecture designed from day one for both local and remote modes.
